cross_family_conclusions: Qwen 14B and 32B have the same two-token state-advance boundary, independent of source size. Treat the prefill→decode cache/position handoff as the Qwen repair target; do not sweep Qwen schedules first.

The generic Llama/Mistral adapter has both correctness and observability gaps. The Llama reference evaluated six prompt tokens while Hawking reported five, making prompt-special-token and cache initialization the first repair surface.
Mistral Small proves --max-stall-ms currently does not bound the no-token prefill condition. Repair the guard before another large generic-adapter invocation.
DeepSeek's dedicated MLA/MoE defect remains independent and already has a per-layer llama.cpp oracle. It should be repaired from that oracle, not from latency output.

No raw adapter passed state advance, so every AUTOTUNE_PROFILE, GRAVITY_ADAPTER, GRAVITY_ORACLE, and RUNG_MEASUREMENT gate remains blocked. This is the intended fail-closed outcome: no false TG claim and no resident GGUF kept merely for speculative tuning.
repair_order: Add a compact, source-SHA-bound multi-token parity fixture for Qwen, generic Llama/Mistral, and DeepSeek. It must gate any autotune invocation.
Fix the generic Llama/Mistral prompt token/BOS and initial KV/position contract; add nonzero device and dispatch accounting before a Mistral profile surface is introduced.
Fix Qwen's prefill-to-decode state handoff against both existing Qwen receipts, then run its existing autotune controls on the repaired 14B source only.
Make the forward watchdog cover prefill as well as decode, then repair DeepSeek from the existing per-layer oracle.
Only after a raw family passes parity should a family-specific Gravity header/tensor map, artifact oracle, and lower-rung pack be built.
